 NEWSFLASH: Anthropic’s shares have started trading, giving the AI pioneer a valuation of $2tn. 
 After more than two hours, Anthropic’s share have begun trading… at a price of $111.50 each.
 That’s 34% more than the $83 at which the company sold its shares in today’s IPO.
 That IPO valued Anthropic at $1.5tn, but now that the shares are actually trading, it’s market capitalisation is up to $2tn.

 34m ago 11.58 EST A 34% ‘pop’ for a newly floated stock is not terribly unusual. 
 And while it suggests Anthropic could have raised more money in its IPO (by selling its shares at a higher price), there are sometimes good reasons not to do that.
 Underwriters often decide to price an IPO below value, to attract buyers and ensure strong demand.
 Dr. Paulina Roszkowska , Lecturer in Finance at Bayes Business School in London, argues that Anthropic’s board was right to “leave something on the table for their new shareholders”, explaining:
 double quotation mark “Resist the temptation to squeeze out the highest possible price. Should an AI correction take 20 or 30 per cent off the shares in 2026/2027, investors will be less forgiving if management sold them perfection.
 “After all, they may well need these investors again. With heavy losses and enormous spending plans, today’s generous valuation could become tomorrow’s fundraising problem. Investors remember who left something on the table and who took the table too.
 Share 40m ago 11.53 EST Anthropic valued at $2tn as shares surge 34% as trading begins
 NEWSFLASH: Anthropic’s shares have started trading, giving the AI pioneer a valuation of $2tn. 
 After more than two hours, Anthropic’s share have begun trading… at a price of $111.50 each.
 That’s 34% more than the $83 at which the company sold its shares in today’s IPO.
 That IPO valued Anthropic at $1.5tn, but now that the shares are actually trading, it’s market capitalisation is up to $2tn.
 Share 48m ago 11.44 EST Anthropic on course to break $2tn barrier as shares are set to soar in debut
 Anthropic appears on course to hit $2tn in market value ⁠as its shares look set to soar in their Nasdaq debut, with investors rushing to own a stake in the world’s first publicly traded frontier AI company.
 The stock was set to open at $111 , 33% higher than the IPO price of $83, according to indications as of 11.44am ET.
 Share Updated at  11.48 EST 1h ago 11.26 EST The day so far: Anthropic could open at $110 a share
 Anthropic has debuted on the US stock market after raising the largest amount of investment in history for an initial public offering. Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei , rang the Nasdaq opening bell. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said. The AI giant, which makes the Claude chatbot, is expected to become one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world at more than $1.5tn, though it was founded just five years ago.
 While the opening price hasn’t been settled just yet, latest data indicated that Anthropic’s shares could open at $110. That would be a significant jump from the $83 at which shares were sold in its IPO last night.
 Anthropic’s listing will serve as a bellwether for the multitrillion-dollar artificial intelligence boom as the first frontier lab to be publicly traded. Wall Street investors and the entire global tech industry – in particular, OpenAI, the parent company of ChatGPT – are watching closely how it fares on the public market.
 Share Updated at  11.29 EST 1h ago 11.20 EST Protesters arrested at the Nasdaq as Anthropic debuts
 Lex McMenamin As Dario Amodei exited Nasdaq MarketSite in Midtown Manhattan after the opening bell celebration, four people were arrested by New York City police for blocking the entrance to the building in protest.
 Two dozen people arrived at 9 am for an action “demand[ing] a freeze to reckless AI development and destruction,” organized by groups including the New York City chapters of Democratic Socialists of America , Jewish Voice for Peace, Climate Defiance, Sunrise Movement, and more.
 “I’m proud to join activists and community members out here today to stand against Anthropic and the tech billionaires who put profit over people,” said New York state senator Aber Kawas , who spoke at the rally. “The American people have made it clear that they’re tired of our government’s endless wars, which are now perpetrated using AI.”
 Share Updated at  11.24 EST 1h ago 11.10 EST Anthropic ’s shares are indicated to open at $107 , Reuters reports.
 Share 1h ago 11.10 EST When SpaceX made its debut in June, Elon Musk ’s satellite, rocket and AI company priced its initial public offering at $135 per share and the stock opened at $150, closing at just under $161 on its first day – a gain of 19%. After peaking at almost $226 a few days later, by early August the price had tumbled to an all-time low of just under $105. It now sits at around $140. We could expect similar volatility here once the hype over Anthropic ’s debut settles down.
 Share 2h ago 10.50 EST Stocks have also fallen further in London, as markets appear to be gripped by a ‘risk off’ mood. 
 The FTSE 100 index is now down 82 points, or -0.8%, at 10,468, extending the six-week low hit earlier today.
 Share 2h ago 10.41 EST View image in fullscreen Dario Amodei, co-founder and CEO of Anthropic leaving after the opening bell ceremony at Nasdaq MarketSite today Photograph: Seth Wenig/AP Share 2h ago 10.36 EST Hmmm the early burst of excitement on the US stock market has rather fizzled out. 
 The Nasdaq Composite is now only up 0.16%, having gained over 1.5% at the start of trading.
 And the Dow Jones Industrial Average , which tracks 30 large US companies, is now in the red, down 0.8%.
 Share 2h ago 10.26 EST Anthropic’s shares are indicated to open at $105!
 Share 2h ago 10.16 EST It’s frustrating, but not at all unusual, to have to wait for a newly floated company to start trading. 
 Newly listed shares do not start publicly trading at the opening bell. Nasdaq and the lead investment banks first gather buy and sell orders, a process that can take several hours for a large listing, the AFP newswire points out.
